title: Release gate: run the qualified binary against a feature of THIS release, with the prior release as the negative control (DEC-204 (b), QCLI-438 precedent)
description:
DEC-204 (OPAG-1419) rules that lore ships prebuilt platform binaries, so the fix rule already applied to quest-cli in QCLI-438 applies here too. This task files the gate half (b) only: no build-identity work.

WHAT WAS MEASURED on origin/dev 35d5ce13. The package-qualification job in .github/workflows/release.yml builds each platform binary from the checkout, and the report records repository.commit by running git rev-parse HEAD in the build job (benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts:505, recorded at :461). The workflow asserts that value equals github.sha (release.yml:617-629, re-asserted at :748-758). It also records platformTarballSha256 (:474) and compares it with a digest recomputed from the same artifact (:748-759); standaloneBinarySha256 (:475) has no consumer anywhere. The binary prints only its version (src/cli.ts:251, src/meta.ts:7) and no commit is embedded in it (benchmark/ladybug/package-build.ts:36-45).

So the gate currently proves the CHECKOUT was at the dispatch commit, and that one artifact survived transport between jobs. It never runs the produced binary to prove it carries this release behavior.

SCOPE. In the release run, the gate must execute the qualified host-platform binary against a feature that exists only in THIS release source tree, and exit nonzero when the binary lacks it. In the same run, the PREVIOUS release published binary runs the same command as the negative control and must fail. Prove both ways: a deliberately stale binary goes red, and a fresh build of the release tree goes green.

The feature is the implementer choice, but it must be a behavior this release actually adds rather than a version string, and its absence must be observable. One shape: a command or flag added by the release, asserted present on the new binary and absent on the previous one.

DEPENDENCY AND PROCESS. This task blocks the pair-release prep (LCLI-714, opum-ai/lore-cli#572), which stays held behind it. It touches CI workflows, so it is on the DEC-182 floor: built on DeepSeek with a Stage 1 review, and opum-doc does an Opus review by ref before landing.

OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately not build work here: the stronger build-identity binding (an embedded commit verified from the binary, or a tarball attestation) and LCLI-482. opum-doc is taking that as a design question.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The release gate runs the qualified host-platform binary against a feature introduced by this release source tree, and the run exits nonzero when the binary lacks that feature.
In the same run, the previous release published binary runs the same command as a negative control, and the gate requires that command to fail.
The gate is proven both ways: a deliberately stale binary produces a red result and a fresh build of the release tree produces a green result, with the evidence for both recorded on this task.
The gate is wired into .github/workflows/release.yml so that no publish can proceed without it.

implementationNotes: Built on DeepSeek, with a Stage 1 review. It touches CI workflows, so it is on the DEC-182 floor: opum-doc does an Opus review by ref before landing.

opum-doc's Opus review of #612 at c5bab0ab (ROUND 1): CHANGES REQUESTED. The fixes are small and the design is right. Do the fixes AFTER the restart; put this in your handoff record verbatim now.
Blocking, fixed in THIS PR, not a follow-up:
1. Anchor the signature. The absent arm must match the exact rejection, the literal `Unrecognized key: "targets"`, with a plain `includes()` on a constant. That also removes the unescaped RegExp (Stage 1 finding 2).
2. A null-status or signal-terminated spawn is NOT measured. The absent arm requires `Number.isInteger(exitCode) && exitCode !== 0`; a null status exits 2 ("nothing measured"), never ok.
3. Pin it: a test that reads release.yml and asserts `publish.needs` contains `release-gate-probe`.
Tests, both ways:
- the anchored signature passes;
- 'targets' in unrelated text with a nonzero exit fails;
- a null status gives exit 2;
- removing release-gate-probe from publish.needs makes the pin test red.
At finalization: the stale comment at release.yml:988 and AC3's evidence on the record.
Then: one new commit (no amend), CI green, report the new head to me. opum-doc reviews the DELTA only (round 2). Land after its verdict, and after the restart.
Kept as opum-doc found them: the qualified-tarball fresh arm, npm latest for the previous arm, both arms in one job, the publish.needs edge, a fail-closed probe with no shell, and the Windows legs not blocking.
The six-minor follow-up shrinks to findings 5 and 6, which are covered at finalization, so it may not be needed. Decide at finalization.

opum-doc's Opus round 2 (delta-only, c5bab0ab..cd9dba44) is APPROVE: reviewer opum-doc on claude-opus-5-5, stamped 2026-10-19T20:43:55Z. Its summary: all three blocking findings FIXED.
1. The anchor was also measured against the published @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64@0.13.0. Its `check` exits 6 with `.lore/agents/documentation.toml does not match agent profile schema 1: Unrecognized key: "targets"`, and `release-gate-probe.mjs --expect absent` against that binary exits 0.
2. The no-status arm exits 2 on both arms, and the real seam reaches "ran".
3. The publish.needs assertion reads the workflow text, with a working mutation control. publish's `if:` is `inputs.publish == true` with no always() or !cancelled(), and there is no continue-on-error, so a red or skipped probe blocks publish.

AC3 EVIDENCE, measured 2026-10-19 after the land (squash 2868648e on origin/dev), on this host, both ways.
STALE BINARY, deliberately the previous release: npm installed @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64@0.13.0 into a scratch prefix (npm/.../bin/lore). Its own `--version` printed 0.13.0. `<bin> check` in this checkout exited 6 with `error: .lore/agents/documentation.toml does not match agent profile schema 1: Unrecognized key: "targets"`. `node scripts/release-gate-probe.mjs --binary <bin> --expect absent --cwd .` exited 0 (the negative control holds). `--expect present` against the same binary exited 1 (RED: a stale binary fails the fresh arm).
FRESH BUILD of the release tree: `bun run build` compiled dist/lore from origin/dev 2868648e. `dist/lore --version` ALSO printed 0.13.0, so a version string alone cannot tell the two byte-sets apart — which is the case DEC-204 (b) exists for. `dist/lore check` exited 0. Probe `--expect present` exited 0 (green); probe `--expect absent` exited 1 (RED: the fresh build cannot stand in as the control).
So a deliberately stale binary produces a red result and a fresh build of the release tree produces a green result, with the gate's own script producing each, in both directions.
finalSummary: Landed in PR opum-ai/lore-cli#612 as squash commit 2868648e on origin/dev; the reviewed head was cd9dba44 (round 2 APPROVE, opum-doc on claude-opus-5-5, 2026-10-19T20:43:55Z). The release.yml release-gate-probe job unpacks the matching-host qualified tarball and installs the previous release from npm latest, then runs both arms in the same job and checkout: --expect present requires the fresh binary to exit 0, --expect absent requires the previous one to exit nonzero carrying the exact rejection `Unrecognized key: "targets"`. publish lists the probe in needs, so no publish can start without both arms. Verified by: both-ways stub tests (anchored literal passes; targets in unrelated text fails; near-miss fails; null status exits 2 on both arms), a test reading release.yml that pins publish.needs with a text-level mutation control, full bun test 5176 pass/4 skip/0 fail, lint, typecheck, lore check, and the two real binaries measured locally (stale 0.13.0: check 6, probe absent 0 / present 1; fresh build: check 0, probe present 0 / absent 1). Finalization also reworded the release.yml comment at 1013-1014 to say the arm carries the exact rejection.
